messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate across rr-us-west-2. Error rate spike to 18% over baseline. Latency p90 -> 3.4s. Paging on-call (devon). Triggers: gateway timeouts + batch queue growth.
Devon (on-call): seeing it, joining. Paging eng-runtime and SRE.
Alex (sre): on it. Metrics look like batcher queue depth rising on scheduler-pool-3, consumer lag increasing. Possible head-of-line blocking.
Devon (on-call): key customers seeing 504s per Kelly. @Kelly can you confirm impact?
Kelly (CSM): CSM: Several customers reported failures in-chat. One enterprise tenant (acme-inc) is getting timeouts on high-concurrency endpoints. They're on Dedicated but routed through the shared gateway. They're flagged as high priority.
Raj (eng-runtime): logs show repeated requeues and worker-side timeouts. Sample from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:07:10Z scheduler: enqueue batch id=0x7f3f size=32
2026-03-15T12:07:11Z worker[3]: process start batch=0x7f3f
2026-03-15T12:07:12Z worker[3]: worker stuck waiting on kv-cache fetch for shard=11
2026-03-15T12:07:14Z gateway: upstream timeout for request id=abc123 status=504
```
Raj (eng-runtime): looks like a quantized-model shard fetch blocking path; KV cache thrashing. Batches waiting on a small set of hot keys -> HOL.
Alex (sre): immediate mitigations we can try: 1) enable shard fallback to replica set B 2) temporarily reduce max-batch-size to lower queue head latency 3) route high-QPS tenants to low-latency pool (if capacity).
Devon (on-call): doing 2) now — lowering max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 on scheduler-pool-3. Running command:
```
# from ops CLI
opsctl scheduler update --pool scheduler-pool-3 --max-batch-size 16
```
Devon (on-call): pushed. Observing queue depth...
(2m) Devon (on-call): queue depth dropping from 420 -> 110. Error rate down to 12%. p95 latency 2.1s.
Devon (on-call): also enabling temporary prefix caching bypass for the hot key set to avoid KV fetch blocking.
Raj (eng-runtime): doing a replica fallback for affected shards:
```
runtime-tool fallback-shard --shard 11 --target replica-b
```
Raj (eng-runtime): fallback triggered; shard 11 now served from replica-b. Monitoring for cache warm-up.
Alex (sre): adding circuit-breaker on gateway route /v1/generate to fail-fast for requests > 250ms queueing to reduce downstream pileup.
Devon (on-call): applied gate rule. Observing: 5xx trending down.
(5m) Kelly (CSM): Customers seeing improvement, but acme-inc reports intermittent 504s during peak. They asked for ETA.
Devon (on-call): ETA: further reduction expected within 10–15m as caches repopulate and batch size change takes full effect. I'll update them.
Alex (sre): root cause hypothesis: scheduler pooling policy + an uneven key distribution created an imbalance. A small hot-key set caused a worker to block on KV fetch (disk or remote), creating head-of-line blocking for larger batches. When backlog grows, gateway timeouts rise.
Raj (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) heatmap of key distribution for last 24h 2) add defensive KV fetch timeout + async fetch to avoid blocking the worker 3) autotune batch size based on queue latency signals.
Devon (on-call): creating incident doc and attaching mitigation timeline.
Devon (on-call): Incident doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1718000000 (placeholder)
Alex (sre): escalation: if error rate doesn't fall below 2% in 20m, we'll initiate a controlled fallback: route high-QPS tenants to dedicated pool or pause bursts.
(12m) Ops Alert Bot: NOTE: autoscaler triggered an extra node in scheduler-pool-4 to help throughput.
Devon (on-call): thanks. Observed improvement: last 5m error rate 1.8%, p95 1.2s.
Kelly (CSM): relaying to acme-inc: we see improvement, keeping watch, please ping if you see anything else. They acknowledged.
Raj (eng-runtime): capturing logs for postmortem. Please include trace ids: abc123, def456, ghi789.
Alex (sre): post-incident action items: - implement adaptive batching policy - add KV fetch non-blocking mode - add routing rule to protect dedicated tenants from shared gateway overload - add automated playbook to reduce batch size and enable replica fallback on KR spikes
Devon (on-call): moving to monitoring phase. Will handoff to next on-call at 13:00 UTC.
Devon (on-call): Handoff: state=stabilized, open actions=3 (see doc). Next on-call: Alex.
Alex (sre): taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem and the follow-ups.
Kelly (CSM): will coordinate customer comms summary and timeline.
Devon (on-call): closing live mitigation. If any regression, reopen thread and page. :white_check_mark:
thread_summary: Incident thread: scheduler pool batch queue growth caused KV-cache blocking and head-of-line delays resulting in elevated 5xx/504s. Mitigations: reduce max_batch_size, enable shard fallback, apply gateway fail-fast, autoscaler added capacity. Stabilized and handed off.
